name: Lost City Hydrothermal Field

sources.title: Lost City Hydrothermal Field — on the Atlantis Massif at 750-900 m: carbonate chimneys up to 60 m (Poseidon), alkaline fluids from serpentinisation
Kelley et al. (2001), An off-axis hydrothermal vent field near the Mid-Atlantic Ridge at 30° N, Nature 412
Kelley et al. (2005), A serpentinite-hosted ecosystem: the Lost City hydrothermal field, Science 307
NOAA Ocean Explorer — Lost City expeditions (chimneys, flanges, fauna)

notes: Built by code (model_sources/Q521459_lost_city.py, tools/meshkit.py, tools/scenekit.py) with AI assistance. The terrace on the top of the Atlantis Massif, about 300 m across, with Poseidon (about 60 m, a massive base with several spires) and some thirty other carbonate chimneys, from slender pinnacles a few metres high to towers of 35 m, with flanges growing from their sides; white and cream where active, grey where extinct; snails and amphipods on the active surfaces, bacterial films, a few fish. The place and shape of each chimney are approximate.
